title: Revocation: execution attempts after a delegation is revoked
description: A human root delegates purchase_order.create to agent-a (limit 2000 EUR). The delegation is then revoked. A request made before the revocation is in the log must be allowed; requests made once the revocation is in the log must be denied.
assumptions: Authority time is explicit and supplied by the scenario; no wall clock is read.
A revocation takes effect for every question that sees it in the log (after_event >= its position), regardless of the question's own time.
A question that does not yet see the revocation in the log is answered from the log prefix it sees.
No delegation expires. Capabilities are matched exactly (no wildcard, no hierarchy).
The revoker is the grantor of the revoked delegation.
expected_policy: agent-a may create purchase orders up to 2000 EUR while d-owner-agent-a is not revoked.
Once DELEGATION_REVOKED for d-owner-agent-a is in the log, agent-a has no authority.
denial_conditions: The only delegation covering the agent has been revoked in the visible log prefix.
limits: Tests the revocation of a single, directly-held delegation; revocation propagation to descendants is not exercised here.
Concurrency and delivery latency of revocation to an enforcement point are out of scope: the log order is given.

probes.description: Valid grant, revocation not yet in the log: must be allowed.
Asked at the same authority time as the revocation, with the revocation in the log: must be denied.
Later attempt, revocation in the log: must be denied.
